Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the UniBank Group third quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up can be found by pressing * then 1 on your telephone keypad. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review UniBank Group's results for the third quarter. With me this morning are Johnathan Reyes, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Risk Officer; David Kim, Chief Credit Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Reyes.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. UniBank Group delivered excellent results in the third quarter, demonstrating the strength of our franchise and our ability to navigate a dynamic market environment.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Expanding our market share
2. Improving our efficiency ratio
3. Strengthening our balance sheet
4. Investing in our people
5. Driving innovation
6. Meeting our ESG goals.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on our key strategic initiatives and progress, macroeconomic outlook and impact, reserve build and release rationale along with coverage ratios, provision for credit losses including drivers and methodology, operating expenses trends and key drivers, and overall company performance highlights.

Let me begin with our key strategic initiatives and the substantial progress we've achieved under our three-pillar framework: accelerating digital transformation, pursuing sustainable growth in high-potential markets, and enhancing resilience via advanced risk and compliance tools. These efforts are positioning UniBank Group as the leading universal bank amid geopolitical strains, ongoing inflation, and fintech challenges. Our strategic investments rose 18% year-over-year to $2.8 billion, already generating returns via better customer gains and efficiency gains.

On digital transformation, we've ramped up AI, machine learning, and open banking APIs for a smooth, personalized client journey. The UniDigital Platform, on a hybrid cloud with AWS and Google Cloud, now serves 28 million active users—a 32% yearly jump—and handles 65% of retail transactions digitally, versus 42% last year. Highlights include the AI-powered Personal Wealth Advisor, which offers customized investment advice using live market info and behavioral data. Outcomes are strong: consumer banking cross-sell rates rose 15% to 3.2 products per client, boosting wealth management fees 12% to $1.4 billion this quarter.

A major achievement was launching Embedded Finance Solutions with Plaid and Adyen partners in Q3, letting non-banks like Shopify-style e-commerce platforms use our lending and payments white-labeled. This produced $450 million in fresh loans in three months, averaging FICO 720+ and losses below 1.2%, better than subprime norms. For business clients, Trade Finance Digitization uses blockchain in an IBM-HSBC style consortium, cutting letter-of-credit times from 10 days to 4 hours. It's at 45% adoption in corporates, adding $800 million in supply chain revenue.

Digital gains shine brightest in APAC, grabbing 22% wallet share via UniPay SuperApp with 15 million monthly users in Southeast Asia, riding the Grab-Gojek cashless wave. In North America, we're CFPB-open banking ready with APIs, outpacing JPMorgan in data ecosystems.

For sustainable growth in promising areas, we're directing capital to emerging markets and green finance. APAC and LatAm expansions came through M&A and new builds. The NeoCredito FinTech buy in Brazil grew to $3.2 billion loans at 24% ROE and 5.8% NIM, helped by Selic hikes. In India, our NBFC joint venture like SBI-YONO added 40% deposits to INR 150 billion ($1.8 billion) via UPI links.

EMEA faces ECB cuts and Basel IV, but we've targeted niches: ESG-Linked Deposits meeting EU SFDR drew €12 billion, 85% from Article 8/9 funds. Sustainable finance is 18% of our $450 billion IB pipeline, up from 9%, with $2.5 billion green bonds for Enel-Ørsted peers. Our Bloomberg-integrated ESG model cut IFRS 9 ECL by 22 bps.

Client wins: 4.2 million net new relationships, up 14%, Gen Z/millennials +28% via gamified 4.5% APY savings beating Ally-SoFi at Fed 5.25-5.50%.

On resilience, $650 million went to cyber defenses. The AI Fraud Detection Engine with graph neural networks cut false positives 37%, stopping $1.2 billion fraud—0.8% of volume, topping FIS-NICE benchmarks. CET1 at 13.2%, +50 bps QoQ, buffers Dodd-Frank and Basel IV.

CBDC program pilots wholesale on Hyperledger with BIS mBridge, PBOC, MAS; $500 million RWA tokenization saved 6.2% on collateral.

These yield NPS 72 vs. J.D. Power 58, opex/revenue to 52% from 58%, P/E to 11.5x on 9% FY24 EPS guide. Next, 20% of $10B capex to AI hubs in Singapore-Tel Aviv for 15-20% non-interest CAGR to 2027. Neobanks like Revolut-Nubank squeeze retail margins, deposit betas 85%, but 42% fee/25% markets revenue protects; mid-teens ROTE by 2026 beating Wells-Santander.

Turning to the macroeconomic outlook and its effects. Our operations span retail, commercial, IB, wealth, markets in 20+ countries, North America, Europe, APAC heavy. Diversification shines here.

Globally, GDP at 3.1% 2024 per IMF, off 3.2% on China demand, supply issues. U.S. core PCE 2.6% nears Fed 2%; funds steady 5.25-5.50%, but 75 bps cuts priced to year-end, first November. ECB cut 75 bps to 3.50% deposit, eurozone 0.8% growth.

Geopolitics: Middle East-Ukraine energy spikes Brent +8% QoQ to $82/bbl; U.S.-China hits exports. U.S. consumer solid, PCE +2.8% YoY, unemployment 3.7%, wages 4.1%.

P&L impacts: NII gained from rates, NIM +25 bps QoQ to 3.45% on commercial loan mix, securities reprice. Loans +4.2% QoQ to $285B, C&I +7% middle-market reshoring CHIPS. Consumer +2.8% selective mortgages at 6.8% 30yr. Deposits $420B sticky, L/D 68%, Apex Mobile 15M users +22% YoY.

Credit top-notch: NPLs 92 bps from 88 bps <1.2% peak, prov $450M or 28 bps loans. CECL reserves 2.1x stress losses +100 bps rates. IB M&A +35% QoQ $220M, $15B tech deals; IPO backlog $8B back-half.

Regions: U.S. 55% earnings, commercial renewables-data centers; ESG lending $50B +40%, green bonds JPM-like. Europe 25%, Germany PMI 42.3 limits loans 1.5%; UK wealth AUM +12% £120B S&P rally. APAC 15%, China property trim CRE 10% to $12B, Alipay 2.5M tx/day; Brazil +9% commodities.

Positioning: $10B swaps lock 4%+ receives, NIM risk <10 bps -200 bps. GenAI fraud with Palantir-ApexShield -40% false positives, $150M scams; BaaS Stripe $80M fees +55%.

2025 GDP U.S. 2.4%, euro 1.2%, ROE 13-14%, CET1 11.8%, LCR 135%. NII Q4 flat+2%, FY EPS $4.85-4.95. Risks oil $100, elections; 42% fee mix aids.

Next, on reserve build/release rationale and coverage ratios. We recorded a modest $175 million provision for credit losses—or loan loss provision—in Q3, a $50 million build from Q1 release, YTD $320 million. This stems from forward-looking CECL under ASC 326.

Rationale: quantitative ECL models (PD, LGD, EAD) showed PD uptick on macro updates—baseline GDP 2.1% 2024 (-20 bps inflation), downturn unemployment 5.8%; plus CRE/middle C&I migrations.

Delinquencies 1.12% from 1.25% Q1, better Wells-Citi; CRE office 4.8% remote-driven, $120M alloc. NCOs 42 bps ann from 38 bps <55 bps 5yr avg.

Qualitative overlays for geopolitics, Red Sea supply on $15B trade finance, regional outflows SVB-like, +15% ECL.

Coverage: ACL $8.7B +2.1% QoQ +8% YoY.
- ACL/loans 1.85% stable QoQ +20 bps YoY > SIB median 1.72% S&P.
- NPL cov 285% on $1.1B NPLs > JPM 210%.
- Criticized/classified 112% on $4.2B, CRE 15.2% >12.8% avg.

Regions: U.S. consumer/retail 2.45% ACL $250B mortgages/cards, delinq 0.9% wages beat inflation, AI origination -10% subprime. Commercial CRE office/multi $90M build $45B, sold $2B 95% recovery >KeyCorp. EMEA $120B IFRS9 Stage3 320%, ECB aids but UK prop overlay. APAC $80B ACL 1.2%, China prop $30M $5B indirect no devs.

Tech: ML CECL with Black Knight alt data mobility/satellite CRE, +18% accuracy; real-time PD cloud Goldman Marquee-like.

Supports 12-15% ROE; diversify C&I 5% IG, fintech Plaid JV 20% low-risk unsecured. Q4 prov $150-250M no recession, cov 1.80-1.90%; stress 10% CRE drop NY Fed. CET1 12.8% LCR 145%.

On provision for credit losses drivers and methodology: Q3 PCL $450M +15% QoQ from $390M Q2, -8% YoY $490M Q3'23. For $1.2T loans, ACL $22.5B 1.88% loans +5 bps QoQ stable YoY; NPL cov 285%.

Drivers: macro 40% QoQ (Fed dot fewer cuts terminal 3.75-4%, PCE 2.6%, unemp 4.3%; stress GDP -0.5% 2025 unemp 5.2% CRE cap 7.5%; CRE office prov +25% $120M JPM-Wells like). Portfolio 35%: consumer $150M cards delinq +45bps 3.2% NYFed, auto subprime 8.1%; $180B consumer NCO 2.85% +20bps YoY; C&I $100M mfg/retail deferral rolloff, mort -10% $40M. Regional 25%: U.S.75% +18% SE/MW CRE spillover Regions-like $50B CRE 12% office multi/indust; Europe15% flat €80M ECB cuts UK office vac 15%; APAC10% -5% A$60M China stim $20B trade no devs. NPL +12% QoQ $7.9B 0.66%, early delinq 1.4%.

Methodology CECL ASC326: pool risk traits FICO/NAICS, DCF life adj prepay. PDxLGDxEAD: PD cycle logistic 20yr data vintage (2019 auto -15% 2021), roll-rates; LGD 42% secured haircut 20% CRE; EAD undrawn 40%. Overlays 3 scen base60% adv30% sev10% VAR unemp beta1.8 GDP1.2 house0.9 MoodyOxford; +10bps Q3 rates. ML gradient boost 500k accts +12% PD vs scorecard COVID test; sat imagery CoreLogic CRE park proxy -8% unc; ind risk validate A-IRB CCAR.

Outlook: CET1 11.8% +220bps min; derisk CRE orig -20% YoY $15B agency MBS IG; EWS DSR<1.25x 70% defaults; AI workout $5B unit. Q4 PCL $420-470M no recess, up $550M unemp>4.5%; ROCE 1.12% top quartile. Liquidity $30B.

Regarding operating expenses trends and key drivers, our non-interest expenses hit $10.2 billion for full-year 2023, +4.2% from $9.8 billion 2022, lagging 7.1% revenue growth. Q3 flat QoQ $2.55B on efficiency wins, adjusted ex $150M FDIC SVB levy Q3.

Categories: Comp/benefits 42% $4.3B +6% YoY: 3.5% merit tech/risk talent war, perf inc orig vols, FTE +1.2% 85k digital/wealth; med/pension +8% JPM-BAC like, var comp 28%. Tech/data 22% $2.2B +12%: $450M cloud 65% AWS/Azure -15% data ctr; Temenos core retail 12 mkt 40M accts STP -30% pays; cyber $350M zero-trust AI threat post-MOVEit; genAI SEC filings/chatbot UniAssist 15M Q4 int +20% compl; ROI 10-12%, tech/rev 18%. Reg/prof fees 15% $1.5B +9%: U.S. Dodd-CECL $120M, Europe PSD3-DORA $200M >HSBC 25% dep share; audit legal M&A Midwest $1.2B buy. Occ/mark/other 21%: occ $1.1B flat 150 branch close 200 digital; mark $800M -2% Google perf high-yield deps +14%; FDIC prem.

Regions: NA65% U.S. +3% Branch2.0 CA wage TX serv, Can +5% OSFI Basel3; Europe20% +8% UK ringfence BaFin Dublin eff; APAC10% +11% Sing dig license India UPI RBI rupee; LatAm5% flat Brazil Pix -25% remit.

Trends: eff ratio 54.2% from 56.1% best large-cap ex-SoFi; exp/FTE $120k -2%; infl adj +1.5% <KBW 2.5%. 2024 growth 3-5% Q1 payroll.

Fit for Growth: ZBB 80% disc, AI auto 10k proc/yr Wells RPA, outsource Genpact India $100M save. Fee pays +15% VisaDir wealth AUM+12% $450B dep beta 35%.

Finally, overall company performance highlights. We posted strong Q3 results beating guides, resilient franchise via deposit growth, digital shift, risk discipline amid rates, geopolitics, CRE soften.

Revenue $14.8B +12% YoY +5% QoQ beat cons $250M; 9th double-digit qtr. NII $9.2B +15%, NIM 3.85% +22 bps. Non-int $5.6B +8%, IB +20% $45B tx $12B tech merger Snowflake-AMD like.

Adj EPS $2.15 +14% >$2.05, ROTCE 18.2% from 16.8% JPM-BAC tier. Shareholder $2.1B div/repur, CET1 12.1% >req div yld 3.2%.

Segments: Consumer/Community 45% rev loans $420B +7% mort/cards +10%, deps $650B +6% core78% app acq 1.2M/q +25%. Comm Bank loans $380B +9% office CRE caut $450M prov $2.5B NPL 0.45% half FDIC avg. IB/Mkts eq trad +30% $1.8B vol Fed cuts FI +12% bond iss; Wealth AUM $1.2T +14% NNM $25B >MS Apex Prime 15% HNW dig.

Regions: U.S.65% rev +13% yields 5.8% Fed5.25-5.50; Europe20% +10% ECB Dublin fund UK deps +18%; APAC15% +16% Sing/HK +12% trade decouple PBOC prop trim.

BS: loans $1.05T +8% C&I11% cons6%; deps $1.4T +7% L/D75% LCR125%. Credit ACL 1.25% loans NPL0.55% -10bps NCO0.28%; CECL stress March crisis ok.

Eff/inno: ratio 52% -200bps $300M synergies consol. FraudGuard NVIDIA-Palantir $1.2B fraud -40% FP; AWS 70% core -50% latency Zelle P2P 15M users; Ripple blockchain APAC $5B Q3 -60% SWIFT.

Fortress BS: fee 38% +6pts ESG $50B green YTD Stripe SMB embed. Q4 rev $15-15.3B EPS2.20-2.25 FY ROTCE18.5%; Fed cuts 60% deps repr 12mo M&A wealth tech.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning. UniBank Group reported net income of $3.2 billion for the third quarter, or $2.15 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 15% due to NIM expansion from higher loan and securities yields alongside steady deposit growth. Non-interest income was up 8% driven by robust investment banking fees and wealth management growth. Our efficiency ratio improved to 52.5%. We are on track to achieve our financial targets for the year.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. From a risk perspective, we are closely monitoring commercial real estate pressures and geopolitical tensions including energy volatility and supply chain issues. We are taking proactive steps to mitigate these risks—such as enhancing AI fraud detection, advancing CBDC pilots, and maintaining overlays in our models—and sustain a strong risk profile with CET1 at 12.5% and LCR above 135%.

David Kim:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains strong with non-performing loans at 0.92% and net charge-offs at 0.42%. We are actively managing our loan portfolio through selective underwriting, derisking CRE, diversifying into IG corporates, and leveraging AI-driven early warnings, and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, instructions for queuing up can be found by pressing * then 1. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on your embedded finance solutions and digital transformation progress, particularly the ROI and regional traction?

Johnathan Reyes:
Good morning, Mike. Absolutely, our embedded finance launch with Plaid and Adyen has been a game-changer, generating $450 million in high-quality originations quickly with superior FICO and low losses. Combined with UniDigital's 28 million users and 65% digital transactions, we've seen cross-sell jumps and 12% fee uplift. In APAC, UniPay's 15 million MAUs capture wallet share, while North America API compliance positions us well. Early ROI is evident in efficiencies and NPS gains, and we're scaling BaaS further for non-interest growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
What is your strategy for deposit growth and managing betas in a potential rate cut environment?

Michael Chen:
Thanks, Emily. Deposits hit record levels at $1.4 trillion, up 7%, with core low-cost at 78% thanks to digital yields and onboarding. Betas are stabilizing around 35-85% depending on segment, insulated by swaps locking 4%+ and diversified revenue. Strategy includes ESG-linked products drawing €12 billion, gamified high-yield accounts for younger clients, and fintech JVs boosting inflows. We're positioned for cuts with 60% repricing soon, guiding sticky growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Singh with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Raj Singh:
How are you addressing CRE exposure and related provisions amid office challenges?

Lisa Patel:
Hi Raj. CRE is a focus, with office at low-single digits of portfolio; we've trimmed originations 20%, sold non-core assets at strong recoveries, and built reserves specifically—$120 million this quarter on targeted allocations. Coverage is robust at 15.2% for CRE criticized, with alt data and stress tests against 10% declines. Diversification to industrial/multifamily and ESG keeps NPLs half industry average, well-buffered.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen:
Can you update us on tech investments ROI, especially AI and cloud migration?

David Kim:
Good morning, Laura. Tech spend up 12% but yielding strong: cloud shift 65-70% cut data costs 15%, Temenos streamlined 40 million accounts -30% processing, AI fraud engines slashed false positives 37-40% stopping $1.2-1.5 billion threats. GenAI chatbots handled millions of queries, blockchain/Ripple saved 60% cross-border. ROI 10-12%, eff ratio sub-54%, supporting ROTCE push to 18%+.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Reyes for any closing remarks.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you for your interest in UniBank Group. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
